headline: Profit growth outpaces revenue as efficiency improves
summary_short: LBX Pharmacy Chain's H1 2026 revenue was ¥10.998B, up 2.07% y/y, while net profit attributable grew faster at +12.3% y/y to ¥447M; Q2 net profit attributable alone grew 24.25% y/y, well ahead of Q2 revenue's 3.32% y/y gain.
summary_long: H1 2026 revenue was ¥10.998B (+2.07% y/y); net profit attributable ¥447M (+12.3% y/y) — profit outgrew revenue. Q2 alone: revenue +3.32% y/y, net profit attributable +24.25% y/y, non-GAAP net profit +27.76% y/y — the profit/revenue gap widened further in Q2. Company attributes this to same-store retail sales acceleration (H1 +3.24% y/y, Q2 +5.27% y/y), online/O2O channel sales of ¥1.774B (+19.06% y/y), and improved store efficiency including inventory turnover down 3 days y/y to 86 days. Network stood at 15,177 stores (9,622 direct, 5,379 franchise) at period end. Q2 standalone EPS of ¥0.24 fell 31.4% q/q.
confidence_notes: No edgarCik; shard sourceLink is a Yahoo fallback. One WebSearch query surfaced comprehensive H1 2026 figures directly; one WebFetch of the Securities Times (证券时报, stcn.com — non-aggregator) recap confirmed and expanded on drivers (same-store sales, O2O channel, inventory turnover, store network). Care taken converting 亿元 (hundred-millions) manually — the fetch tool's own summary mislabeled 109.98亿元 as '109.98 billion' (should be ¥10.998B) and 4.47亿元 as '4.47 billion' (should be ¥447M); corrected here. Q2 standalone net-profit growth (+24.25% y/y) is stated as a rate only — no absolute Q2 net-profit yuan figure was disclosed in the source, so that KPI row's value is 'n/a'. EPS row is the Q2-standalone actual from resolve-earnings-target.mjs's shard KPIs (Yahoo earningsChart) and is not on the same cumulative basis as the H1 revenue/profit rows.

drivers.explanation: Same-store retail sales accelerated sequentially (H1 +3.24% y/y, Q2 +5.27% y/y) and online/O2O channel sales grew 19.06% y/y to ¥1.774B.
Store efficiency improved, with inventory turnover down 3 days y/y to 86 days, aided by supply-chain and automation tooling.
